To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

boron carbide-based pyrotechnic compositions containing potassium chloride as a diluent and calcium stearates as a lubricant produce copious amounts of smoke and are suitable for use as end-burning smoke grenade compositions.

the addition of 2 wt % calcium stearate to boron carbide‐based smoke compositions reduces the burning rate from about 0.5 cm s-1 to about 0.09 cm s- 1, that potassium chloride is a good diluent for boron carbide smoke compositions, and that the addition of potassium chloride to a boron carbide-based smoke composition reduces incandescence and slag formation while producing copious amounts white smoke.

boron carbide‐based smoke compositions containing 25–30 wt-% potassium chloride and 2 wt-% calcium stearnate produce copious amounts of visually effective, white smoke and outperform the US military's in-service smoke grenade, the M83 TA, both qualitatively (visual obscuration) and quantitatively (smoke output).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new smoke compositions that can be used in end-burning smoke grenade applications, and the results of this research have led to a new generation of end-burning smoke compositions.
developing a boron carbide–based composition that can be loaded into the existing M83 grenade can.
the development of a boron carbide-based smoke composition that is capable of producing a high-quality smoke cloud with a high photopic mass-based figure of merit and a low luminosity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental compositions described here are a viable replacement for the M83 TA grenade.
the addition of calcium stearate as a lubricant and the use of potassium chloride as a diluent are effective ways of improving the performance of boron carbide‐based smoke compositions.
the boron carbide‐based smoke composition containing KCl-30 is the best composition for the M83 grenade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the boron carbide-based compositions are a viable alternative to the currently used aluminum-based compositions.
boron carbide is a promising new ingredient for visual obscuration pyrotechnic formulations.
the addition of potassium chloride to boron carbide-based smoke compositions reduces incandescence, increases slag formation, and increases white smoke output.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of boron carbide as an oxidizer in smoke compositions can lead to improved smoke quality and quantity, and that the addition of calcium stearate is an effective method for slowing the rate of combustion in end-burning grenades.
boron carbide is an excellent smoke-generating material that is capable of producing high-quality smoke in the presence of a suitable diluent.

the addition of just a few percent of a suitable lubricant to a boron carbide‐based smoke composition can reduce the burning rate to a range that allows the smoke to burn in an end-burning grenade can.
